v8_verdict.status: CEILING — MARGINAL VALUE, BELOW BUYER-GRADE THRESHOLD
v8_verdict.rationale: V8 attacked the L3d derivative mechanism with 10 harsh disturbances (5 favorable, 4 adversarial, 1 combined). Result: derivative shows MARGINAL value — 9.9% M2 (over-drainage) reduction vs C3, dominates in 5/10 states, no catastrophic failures. BUT: 0% M4 (dangerous events) reduction, -1.1% M1 (WORSE on time-outside-target), 62.9% drainage preserved (below 75%), and only 5/10 states (below 6 needed for buyer-grade, above 4 for milestone but without the 15% improvement needed). Per CEO directive: 'L3d survives only if it demonstrates a reproducible technical advantage against C3 under hostile conditions.' The derivative mechanism does NOT demonstrate a reproducible buyer-grade technical advantage. It shows marginal over-drainage reduction but no improvement on dangerous events and slight regression on time-outside-target. This is a genuine CEILING — the derivative mechanism is NOT sufficiently valuable to justify a standalone invention.
v8_verdict.comparison_to_v7: V7 showed L5 (predictive) has CEILING — does not outperform C3. V8 shows L3d (derivative) also has CEILING — marginal value (9.9% M2 reduction), not buyer-grade. BOTH mechanisms in Territory #4 have now been attacked and found insufficient against C3 (instantaneous ΔP). The venous-aware differential (C3) itself remains valuable vs C2 (P_CSF only) — but that is L2 territory, already taught by WO2020086847A1 + US 7,691,077 + Azygos patents. NOT novel.
